cards.headline: Missing: 15-year-old boy last seen in Tampines
bullets: Police are looking for 15-year-old Danial Matin Nor Azam, who has gone missing.
He was last seen around Tampines Avenue 9 early on August 22.
He was wearing a black hoodie and dark shorts when last spotted.
Anyone with information can contact the police hotline.

cards.headline: Missing: 62-year-old woman last seen in Tampines
bullets: Police are looking for 62-year-old Fazidah Ansan, missing since late August 22.
She was last seen near Block 499A Tampines Avenue 9.
She was wearing a beige headscarf, black blouse and beige pants.

cards.headline: As bicycle accidents hit 4-year high, cyclists call for more mutual respect from peers, road users
bullets: Bike accidents hit a four-year high with 772 cases in 2025.
Over half of these accidents happened because cyclists rode carelessly or didn't look properly.
Cyclists and other road users are blaming each other for unsafe roads.
Some cyclists break traffic rules, expecting others to give way.
There's a call for more respect among all road users.

cards.headline: Work stress led woman to discover  genetic condition that looks like heart attack
bullets: A woman's work stress led to symptoms that mimicked a heart attack.
Doctors initially diagnosed her with irregular heartbeat, a common heart rhythm disorder.
Further checks revealed she had a genetic condition causing her heart muscle to thicken.
This condition, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, can lead to serious heart problems if untreated.
She is managing her condition well with medication and did not need surgery.

cards.headline: NUS researchers find drug that turns off ‘master switch’ in aggressive breast cancer
bullets: NUS researchers found a drug that shrinks aggressive breast cancer tumours by about 90%.
The drug targets a 'master switch' called DP103 that helps cancer grow and spread.
In lab tests, the drug reduced cancer stem cells by up to 60%.
This could lead to more personalised treatments for a difficult-to-treat cancer subtype.

cards.headline: Raised differently, united by food: The couple making Singapore food heritage part of everyday life
bullets: A couple runs Sendok Rakyat, using food to connect people with Singapore's heritage.
They host workshops teaching traditional dishes like nasi ulam and sharing stories.
Participants learn about ingredients, their history, and personal food memories.
The group explores how different food traditions have mixed in Singapore.
They believe food is a powerful way to start conversations about identity and belonging.

cards.headline: ‘Being a player is my passion’: Keisuke Honda targets Singapore Premier League title with FC Jurong
bullets: Football star Keisuke Honda will play for FC Jurong in the Singapore Premier League.
Honda aims to lead FC Jurong to win the league title this season.
He was officially unveiled as a player at Jurong East Stadium.
Honda also wants to gain more experience to become Japan's national team coach.

cards.headline: Pre-peak discount issue that affected 210,000 journeys a day on Aug 20 and 21 fixed: SimplyGo
bullets: SimplyGo fixed a glitch that missed pre-peak discounts for 210,000 daily train trips on Aug 20-21.
A setup error meant SimplyGo EZ-Link and bank card users didn't get their usual fare savings.
Commuters can now see correct fares with discounts applied in the SimplyGo app.
The pre-peak discount offers up to 50 cents off for weekday travel before 7:45 am.

cards.headline: A dinner that's also a play at Michelin-starred Nouri, where chef Ivan Brehm turns actor as you eat
bullets: Restaurant Nouri is offering a 10-course meal that's also a play about chef Ivan Brehm's life.
The three-hour dining experience costs S$348++ and runs until August 30.
Each dish is paired with a chapter of the chef's personal journey, told through acting.
The play, 'A Matter Of Taste', is a collaboration between Nouri and Checkpoint Theatre.

cards.headline: Commentary: Don’t settle for easy explanations after a pat on a child’s head turns into shoving incident
bullets: Police are investigating a father who allegedly shoved an elderly man after he patted the man's daughter.
The incident highlights different views on personal boundaries and parenting styles.
Children are taught about personal boundaries and consent from a young age.
Parents must teach children how to handle boundary crossings, not just avoid them.
How parents react to boundary crossings teaches children valuable lessons.

cards.headline: Marathon runners are training for a hotter world
bullets: Runners are buying special gear like cooling headbands to cope with hot weather.
Many runners are changing their training plans because of rising temperatures.
Coaches now advise runners to slow down or run at different times when it's hot.
Some athletes are using saunas to get their bodies used to the heat.

cards.headline: Arsenal sweep Coventry aside 3-0 to start title defence with a bang
bullets: Arsenal beat Coventry 3-0 in their first match of the season.
Goals were scored by Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka, and Martin Odegaard.
New signing Christos Tzolis impressed on his league debut.
Coventry City is back in the Premier League after 25 years.

cards.headline: Suzuki e Vitara review: A ‘vestigial organ’ tells you what you need to know
bullets: The Suzuki e Vitara costs S$169,888 with COE, making it pricey against Chinese rivals.
It has a shorter range of 345 km compared to competitors offering 420 km or more.
The electric Suzuki feels familiar to drive, with physical buttons and a quiet ride.
It offers decent space and strong air-con but lacks modern features like wireless charging.
The car requires manual shutdown, unlike many newer electric vehicles.

cards.headline: Upbeat outlook for CDL, UOL after strong H1 earnings, but analysts turn cautious on PropNex, Apac Realty
bullets: CDL's profit jumped over 230% to S$301.6 million in the first half of the year.
UOL's profit rose 23% to S$252.2 million in the same period.
PropNex and Apac Realty saw profits fall as new property launches decreased.
Analysts are positive on CDL and UOL due to upcoming projects and reviews.
Real estate agencies PropNex and Apac Realty face a less optimistic outlook.

cards.headline: Frasers Property partners Malaysia’s Tan & Tan to develop 5-ha mixed project in Petaling Jaya
bullets: Frasers Property and Tan & Tan will build a 5.15-hectare mixed project in Malaysia.
The project, called PJ Quarter, will be built in two phases.
The first phase will include homes, shops, and a park.
Homes in the first phase will go on sale next year.

cards.headline: S'pore teen, 18, bravely helps save grandfather & grandson from Buangkok flat fire
bullets: An 18-year-old neighbour used a fire extinguisher to help fight a blaze in a Buangkok flat.
He also rescued a grandfather and grandson from the burning unit.
The fire started in a bedroom and spread to its contents.
One person was sent to the hospital, and the cause is being investigated.

cards.headline: HK woman, 33, dies after being mauled by 30kg dog at animal shelter she ran
bullets: A 33-year-old woman died after being attacked by a 30kg dog at an animal shelter she ran.
The attack happened after she tried to put the dog into a cage following feeding.
The dog had been brought to the shelter for adoption.
The woman was found with severe injuries to her head, neck, and arms.

cards.headline: M'sian man, 23, allegedly takes his life after going through breakup, mother posts heartbreaking tribute
bullets: A 23-year-old Malaysian man was found dead in Johor Bahru after being reported missing.
His mother believes he died by suicide after a recent breakup.
The man disappeared suddenly after going to lunch with colleagues.
His mother posted a heartfelt tribute online, expressing her grief and confusion.

cards.headline: Starbucks Is Launching A New Mofusand Collab, Featuring Blind Box Keychains & Freebies Up For Grabs
bullets: Starbucks is launching a new Mofusand collection on August 25th.
The collection includes Singapore-exclusive items like wristlets and plush keychains.
You can also get blind box keychains with cat designs.
Spend $25 on delivery orders to get a free Mofusand cup sleeve.

cards.headline: Scoot Will Fly Directly To Guiyang From October, Visit The Chiang Mai Of China From Just $158
bullets: Scoot will fly direct to Guiyang from October 26, with one-way fares starting at $158.
The flight from Singapore to Guiyang takes about 4 hours.
Guiyang is known as a 'Forest City' with mountains and waterfalls.
Scoot will fly to Guiyang three times a week.
Tickets go on sale August 20.

cards.headline: Popular Bookstore’s Jurong Point Outlet Is Closing Down, With Storewide Discounts Of Up To 90% Off
bullets: Popular Bookstore's Jurong Point branch closes on September 13 after 31 years.
The store is having a closing down sale with discounts up to 90% off.
You can get Disney Paint by Number sets at 3 for $10.
Sanrio water bottles are now $10, down from $19.90.
School bag bundles are going for $29.90 instead of up to $68.70.
